functions.name: CLD2::DetectLanguage
functions.signature: CLD2::Language CLD2::DetectLanguage(const char* buffer, int buffer_length, bool is_plain_text, bool* is_reliable)
functions.description: Detects the most likely language of the given UTF-8 text. Skips HTML tags and expands entities unless is_plain_text is true. Returns the primary Language; sets is_reliable true if the top choice is sufficiently above alternatives. For empty input returns UNKNOWN_LANGUAGE; for very short indeterminate text defaults to ENGLISH (for backward compatibility).
requirements: buffer must point to interchange-valid UTF-8 bytes; may contain HTML unless is_plain_text is true
buffer_length must be >= 0 and must not exceed the actual accessible bytes at buffer
is_plain_text controls whether HTML tags/entities are processed (true = treat as plain text, no tag skipping)
is_reliable must be a non-null pointer to a bool for the result
Thread-safe usage is intended by design

functions.name: CLD2::DetectLanguageSummary
functions.signature: CLD2::Language CLD2::DetectLanguageSummary(const char* buffer, int buffer_length, bool is_plain_text, CLD2::Language* language3, int* percent3, int* text_bytes, bool* is_reliable)
functions.description: Detects the top three languages present in the given UTF-8 text and their approximate percentages. Skips HTML tags and expands entities unless is_plain_text is true. language3[0] is usually the return value. text_bytes reports the number of non-tag, letters-only bytes analyzed. For very short indeterminate text defaults to ENGLISH (rather than UNKNOWN_LANGUAGE) for compatibility.
requirements: buffer must point to interchange-valid UTF-8 text
buffer_length must be >= 0 and not exceed the accessible size of buffer
is_plain_text controls HTML handling (true = no tag/entity processing)
language3 must be a non-null pointer to an array with capacity for at least 3 CLD2::Language entries
percent3 must be a non-null pointer to an array with capacity for at least 3 ints; each value will be in the range 0..100
text_bytes must be a non-null pointer to int to receive the count of analyzed non-tag text bytes
is_reliable must be a non-null pointer to bool to receive reliability flag

functions.name: CLD2::ExtDetectLanguageSummary
functions.signature: CLD2::Language CLD2::ExtDetectLanguageSummary(const char* buffer, int buffer_length, bool is_plain_text, CLD2::Language* language3, int* percent3, int* text_bytes, bool* is_reliable)
functions.description: Detects the top three extended languages (includes additional interface languages and single-language scripts) in the given UTF-8 text. Skips HTML unless is_plain_text is true. language3[0] is usually the return value. Unlike the basic APIs, this extended version may return UNKNOWN_LANGUAGE when confidence is insufficient.
requirements: buffer must point to interchange-valid UTF-8 text
buffer_length must be >= 0 and not exceed accessible size
is_plain_text controls HTML handling (true = no tag/entity processing)
language3 must be a non-null pointer to an array with capacity for at least 3 CLD2::Language entries
percent3 must be a non-null pointer to an array with capacity for at least 3 ints; values 0..100
text_bytes must be a non-null pointer to int to receive non-tag text byte count
is_reliable must be a non-null pointer to bool

functions.name: CLD2::DetectLanguageVersion
functions.description: Returns a static version string describing the detector code and data, formatted as "code_version - data_build_date". Useful for diagnostics and logging.
requirements: No arguments; simply call to obtain a NUL-terminated C string
Returned pointer refers to immutable storage and must not be freed

functions.name: CLD2::DumpResultChunkVector
functions.signature: void CLD2::DumpResultChunkVector(FILE* f, const char* src, CLD2::ResultChunkVector* resultchunkvector)
functions.description: Debug helper that prints the contents of a ResultChunkVector to the given FILE stream, optionally labeled by src. Useful for inspecting chunk boundaries and detected languages.
requirements: f must be a valid FILE* opened for writing
src may be NULL or a descriptive label for the source buffer
resultchunkvector must be a non-null pointer to a valid CLD2::ResultChunkVector populated by detection

functions.name: CLD2::loadData
functions.description: Dynamic-mode only: Loads detector data from the specified file path. If other data is already loaded, it is discarded and the file is read again. Until data is loaded, language detection will always fail and return UNKNOWN_LANGUAGE.
requirements: Available only when compiled with CLD2_DYNAMIC_MODE defined
fileName must be a non-null path to a readable data file containing CLD2 model data
Call this before calling any detection functions in dynamic mode to enable detection
Subsequent calls replace previously loaded data

functions.name: CLD2::unloadData
functions.description: Dynamic-mode only: Unloads previously loaded detector data. After this call, language detection will no longer work and will always return UNKNOWN_LANGUAGE until new data is loaded.
requirements: Available only when compiled with CLD2_DYNAMIC_MODE defined
Should be called when detector data is no longer needed or before reinitialization steps as desired
After calling, detection APIs will return UNKNOWN_LANGUAGE until loadData is called again

functions.name: CLD2::isDataLoaded
functions.description: Dynamic-mode only: Returns true if data has been successfully loaded via loadData and not subsequently unloaded. Use to guard detection calls in dynamic mode.
requirements: Available only when compiled with CLD2_DYNAMIC_MODE defined
No arguments; simply call to query whether detector data is currently loaded

data_types.description: A byte sequence representing interchange-valid UTF-8 encoded text. May include printable ASCII characters, tabs, and newlines; can also include HTML markup if not treated as plain text. The buffer is consumed as text for language detection.

import random from typing import List # This generator produces interchange-valid UTF-8 text tailored to exercise # CLD2 language-detection fuzzers. It creates varied content including: # - Single-language passages (English, Spanish, French, German, Italian) # - Non-Latin scripts (Russian, Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Chinese, Japanese) # - Mixed-language documents with proportions # - HTML vs plain text variants, including tags, attributes, entities, comments, scripts/styles # - Short/empty inputs and boundary-size inputs # - Repetitions, punctuation, numbers, whitespace patterns # All outputs are valid UTF-8 and <= 4096 bytes. ASCII_WHITESPACE = [" ", "\t", "\n"] # Small corpora snippets per language/script to bias detection toward that language. LANG_SNIPPETS = { "en": [ "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.", "This is a sample English text for language detection.", "Numbers 12345 and punctuation, commas, and periods.", ], "es": [ "El zorro marrón rápido salta sobre el perro perezoso.", "Este es un texto de ejemplo en español para detección de idioma.", "¿Cómo estás? ¡Buenos días!", ], "fr": [ "Le vif renard brun saute par-dessus le chien paresseux.", "Ceci est un texte d'exemple en français pour la détection de langue.", "À bientôt; merci beaucoup.", ], "de": [ "Falsches Üben von Xylophonmusik quält jeden größeren Zwerg.", "Dies ist ein deutscher Beispieltext zur Spracherkennung.", "Straßen, Grüße, Größen und Zahlen 9876.", ], "it": [ "Ma la volpe col suo balzo ha raggiunto il quieto Fido.", "Questo è un testo di esempio in italiano per il rilevamento della lingua.", "Perché? Sì, certo!", ], "ru": [ "Съешь же ещё этих мягких французских булок, да выпей чаю.", "Это пример текста на русском языке для определения языка.", ], "el": [ "Ξεσκεπάζω την ψυχοφθόρα βδελυγμία.", "Αυτό είναι ένα δείγμα ελληνικού κειμένου για ανίχνευση γλώσσας.", ], "ar": [ "صِفْ خَلْقَ خَوْدٍ كَمِثْلِ الشَّمْسِ إِذْ بَرَزَتْ", "هذا نص عربي تجريبي لاختبار كشف اللغة.", ], "he": [ "דג סקרן שט בים מאוכזב ולפתע מצא חבר.", "זהו טקסט דוגמה בעברית לצורך זיהוי שפה.", ], "zh": [ "中文示例文本用于语言检测，快速的棕色狐狸跳过了懒狗。", "这是一个用于测试的中文段落，其中包含常用汉字。", ], "ja": [ "素早い茶色の狐がのろまな犬を飛び越える。", "これは言語検出のための日本語サンプルテキストです。", ], } HTML_ENTITIES = ["&", "<", ">", """, "'", "©", "😀"] HTML_TAGS = [ ("p", True), ("div", True), ("span", True), ("b", False), ("i", False), ("a", True), ("script", True), ("style", True), ("h1", True), ("ul", True), ("li", True), ] def _rand(r: random.Random, arr: List[str]): return arr[r.randrange(len(arr))] def _make_sentence(r: random.Random, lang: str) -> str: base = _rand(r, LANG_SNIPPETS[lang]) # Add some variability: numbers, punctuation, whitespace extras = [] if r.random() < 0.5: extras.append(str(r.randint(0, 999999))) if r.random() < 0.5: extras.append(_rand(r, [",", ";", ":", ".", "!", "?", "—"])) if r.random() < 0.5: extras.append(_rand(r, ASCII_WHITESPACE)) if extras: base = base + " " + " ".join(extras) return base def _block_for_lang(r: random.Random, lang: str, min_sent=1, max_sent=5) -> str: n = r.randint(min_sent, max_sent) return " ".join(_make_sentence(r, lang) for _ in range(n)) def _wrap_html(r: random.Random, text: str) -> str: # Randomly wrap in nested tags, include attributes and entities, comments, scripts/styles parts = [] # Optional doctype and head if r.random() < 0.5: parts.append("") parts.append("") if r.random() < 0.7: parts.append("") if r.random() < 0.6: parts.append("") if r.random() < 0.4: parts.append("" + _rand(r, ["Test", "Título", "Titre", "Тест"]) + "") # Optional style if r.random() < 0.5: parts.append("") parts.append("") parts.append("") # Insert anchor with entity and attribute if r.random() < 0.7: parts.append("" + _rand(r, HTML_ENTITIES) + "") # Comments and whitespace if r.random() < 0.6: parts.append("") # Core content split into paragraphs or divs wrapper = _rand(r, ["p", "div", "section"]) if r.random() < 0.8 else None if wrapper: parts.append(f"<{wrapper} class=\"c\">") parts.append(text) # Randomly interleave entities for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)): insert_pos = r.randrange(len(parts)) parts.insert(insert_pos, _rand(r, HTML_ENTITIES)) parts.append(f"") else: parts.append(text) # Optional script/style blocks that should be skipped when is_plain_text=false if r.random() < 0.5: parts.append("") if r.random() < 0.5: parts.append("") # List with items if r.random() < 0.5: parts.append("
    ") for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)): parts.append("
  • " + _rand(r, HTML_ENTITIES) + "
    • ") parts.append("
") parts.append("") parts.append("") return "".join(parts) def _mixed_text(r: random.Random) -> str: # Compose a document mixing several languages with random proportions langs = list(LANG_SNIPPETS.keys()) r.shuffle(langs) count = r.randint(2, min(5, len(langs))) chosen = langs[:count] weights = [r.random() for _ in chosen] total = sum(weights) weights = [w / total for w in weights] blocks = [] for lang, w in zip(chosen, weights): # Map weight to number of sentences num = max(1, int(w * 10) + r.randint(0, 2)) blocks.append(_block_for_lang(r, lang, min_sent=num, max_sent=num + 2)) # Interleave separators and whitespace sep = _rand(r, ["\n\n", " ", "\t\n"]) text = sep.join(blocks) # Add a header/footer with different language sometimes if r.random() < 0.4: header_lang = _rand(r, list(LANG_SNIPPETS.keys())) text = _block_for_lang(r, header_lang, 1, 2) + sep + text if r.random() < 0.4: footer_lang = _rand(r, list(LANG_SNIPPETS.keys())) text = text + sep + _block_for_lang(r, footer_lang, 1, 2) return text def _single_lang_text(r: random.Random) -> str: lang = _rand(r, list(LANG_SNIPPETS.keys())) return _block_for_lang(r, lang, 2, 7) def _short_or_empty(r: random.Random) -> str: # Trigger empty/short-path behavior choice = r.random() if choice < 0.33: return "" # empty -> UNKNOWN_LANGUAGE elif choice < 0.66: return _rand(r, ["a", "I", "OK", "no", "sí", "ок"]) # very short else: return _rand(r, ["&", "", " ", "\n\n"]) # tags/entities def _html_or_plain(r: random.Random, core_text: str) -> str: # Sometimes wrap as HTML, sometimes keep plain; include entities optionally if r.random() < 0.55: return _wrap_html(r, core_text) # Plain text with some entities sprinkled s = core_text for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)): pos = r.randrange(len(s) + 1) s = s[:pos] + _rand(r, HTML_ENTITIES) + s[pos:] return s def _truncate_to_limit(s: str, max_bytes: int = 4096) -> str: # Ensure UTF-8 boundary safety by encoding and truncating on codepoint boundary b = s.encode('utf-8') if len(b) <= max_bytes: return s # Truncate safely b = b[:max_bytes] # Back up to the start of a UTF-8 sequence # Continuation bytes are 0b10xxxxxx; find first non-continuation from the end i = len(b) while i > 0 and (b[i-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80: i -= 1 # If we ended in the middle of a multi-byte lead that is incomplete, drop the lead too # Validate minimal UTF-8 by attempting decode progressively while i > 0: try: return b[:i].decode('utf-8') except UnicodeDecodeError: i -= 1 # skip continuation sequences until a safe boundary while i > 0 and (b[i-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80: i -= 1 return "" # fallback def generate(seed: int) -> bytes: r = random.Random(seed) # Choose a scenario scenario = r.random() if scenario < 0.15: core = _short_or_empty(r) elif scenario < 0.5: core = _single_lang_text(r) else: core = _mixed_text(r) # Decide HTML vs plain wrapping and add variability text = _html_or_plain(r, core) # Add leading/trailing whitespace and punctuation noise if r.random() < 0.6: text = _rand(r, ASCII_WHITESPACE) * r.randint(0, 3) + text if r.random() < 0.6: text = text + _rand(r, ASCII_WHITESPACE) * r.randint(0, 3) if r.random() < 0.4: text = ("#" * r.randint(0, 5)) + text if r.random() < 0.4: text = text + ("." * r.randint(0, 5)) # Optionally repeat blocks to increase size while staying under limit if r.random() < 0.4: repeats = r.randint(1, 4) sep = _rand(r, ["\n", " ", "\n\n"]) if r.random() < 0.7 else "" text = sep.join([text] * repeats) # Constrain to 4096 bytes and ensure valid UTF-8 text = _truncate_to_limit(text, 4096) return text.encode('utf-8')
